Subject: Capacity + Unit-Econ walkthrough: read-ahead and sync request

Team —

Ahead of the QBR next week I put together a compact read-ahead so leadership has a single place to review the capacity assumptions and unit-econ levers we'll present to the execs and Lumos Health (their renewal is in the same window). Key ask: please review the attached model and GPU-util trends and flag anywhere you think the assumptions are optimistic (esp. batching/caching benefits, evictions for KV cache).

Read-ahead highlights (very short):
- Current committed GPU pool: 96 x A100-equivalent (shared mix of p4/p5). We model 14% QoQ user growth.
- Baseline utilization (tokens/sec) assumed at 48% average across serving pools; burst headroom 25% available via dedicated burst policy.
- Batching + prefix/KV caching expected to reduce per-token GPU time by ~18% on retrieval-heavy flows and up to 30% for high prefix-reuse chat flows.
- Quantization path (int8 candidates) reduces memory pressure but shows ~4–6% latency tail increase for long-seq prompts in current kernel set.

Specific asks:
1) Lauren — pull the leadership bullets you want highlighted; I'm proposing two slides: runway risk (cost vs demand) and mitigation levers (batching, idle consolidation, temporary spot-backed scale).
2) Marissa — can you sanity-check the model's assumed throughput lift from the batching experiment (sheet tab: batching_sensitivity)?
3) Rishi/Vivek — confirm whether the SLAs we propose to Lumos (p95 < 300ms for endpoint X under dedicated capacity) are acceptable politically and if there are any approval steps for credits.

Attachments: capacity model (xlsx), GPU trends (pdf), read-ahead notes (txt).

Thanks — short sync tomorrow at 10am PT would let us close on bullets. If that doesn't work, I'll send a 30-min slot that works across timezones.

—Sean

Sean — quick read, added comments in the model and uploaded an updated tab (batching_sensitivity_v2). Short summary of what I changed:
- Reduced optimistic batching uplift on mixed workloads from 30% to 22% for production-like request patterns where session affinity keeps KV cache hit low for ~15% of active sessions.
- Modeled a conservative eviction policy that increases cold-start tail by ~3% for ephemeral sessions — I flagged this on the latency sheet.
- Included a short section on spot-backed burst risks (sheet: spot_risk) — if we lean on spot for short bursts we should have a runbook to migrate long-running jobs to reserved capacity to avoid preemption during peak commit windows.

Attachments: 20280402_capacity_model_v3.xlsx (updated).

I also reached out to Lumos to confirm expected concurrency profile this summer — Nora said they'll send a short profile by EOD tomorrow.

Thank you all — clear and actionable. A few executive points to land before the QBR deck is finalized: 

1) Executive summary (one-liner): we have capacity headroom in the near term but must prioritize three programmatic levers to keep unit cost stable as demand scales: (a) targeted batching & prefix-KV caching for high-reuse apps, (b) short-term spot-backed burst with runbook, (c) prioritized dedicated pools for enterprise renewals.
2) Risk callouts: if batching uplift underperforms by more than 10ppt versus our conservative estimate, runway cash burn increases ~18% on the modeled cohort. Make sure that range is visible in the appendix.
3) Ask for Lumos: commit to a 12-month modest dedicated pool (size TBD) with a staged scale plan tied to measured latency & success metrics. Finance team will draft a pricing band; include that as a confidential appendix only.

I'll consolidate these into a one-page exec memo and drop a draft in the Drive link (see HubSpot/Drive links above). Please mark any redlines in the shared doc by EOD Thursday.

-Rishi
